title: Execution Trace Cache
decision: Replace the conventional L1 instruction cache with an Execution Trace Cache that stores decoded micro-operations in dynamic execution order
alternatives_or_rejected: A conventional instruction cache storing raw x86 instruction bytes that must be decoded on every fetch
rationale: x86 instruction decode is complex and limits how many instructions can be fetched and decoded per cycle; caching already-decoded micro-ops in execution order removes the decode bottleneck and increases effective fetch bandwidth
outcome: The front end can deliver multiple decoded micro-ops per cycle without decode latency, though with added complexity in trace line construction and branch handling within traces

title: Hyper-Pipelined Technology
decision: Implement a deeply pipelined architecture with on the order of 20 pipeline stages to maximize clock frequency
alternatives_or_rejected: A shorter pipeline similar to the Pentium III (P6 microarchitecture) that would incur lower branch misprediction penalties but achieve a lower peak clock frequency
rationale: Process technology trends and performance requirements favored maximizing clock frequency; a deeper pipeline reduces the amount of logic per stage, allowing higher operating frequencies
outcome: Initial products operated at 1.4–1.5 GHz with architectural headroom toward higher frequencies, but with a branch misprediction penalty of roughly 20 cycles

title: Rapid Execution Engine
decision: Run the primary integer ALUs at twice the core clock frequency (double-pumped) so they can execute simple integer operations at an effective rate of two per clock cycle
alternatives_or_rejected: Adding more single-pumped ALUs to increase issue width, or accepting lower integer throughput
rationale: Simple integer operations such as add, compare, and branch are extremely common; double-pumping achieves higher throughput without the die area and power cost of duplicating full execution units
outcome: High integer performance for simple operations, with the constraint that more complex operations still require a full clock cycle

title: Branch prediction investment for deep pipeline
decision: Invest in a large Branch Target Buffer and aggressive branch prediction logic to minimize mispredictions given the deep pipeline
alternatives_or_rejected: A smaller predictor or less aggressive speculation that would be insufficient given the ~20 cycle misprediction penalty
rationale: With a deeply pipelined design, each branch misprediction costs many cycles of wasted execution; accurate prediction is therefore critical to achieving good overall performance despite the frequency benefits of the deep pipeline
outcome: Prediction accuracy high enough to make the deep pipeline profitable on typical code, though mispredictions remain a significant performance limiter

title: Large out-of-order execution window
decision: Implement a large out-of-order execution window with a substantial reorder buffer and many in-flight instructions to tolerate latencies
alternatives_or_rejected: A smaller instruction window that would stall more frequently on cache misses and branch resolution in the deep pipeline
rationale: The deep pipeline and high clock frequency make cache miss latencies (in cycles) appear much larger; a large window is necessary to keep execution units busy during long-latency memory operations
outcome: Sustained execution throughput despite cache misses and branch resolution delays
